name: Status Panel
description: Selected-session model, configured effort, workspace policy, git, context and token counters, with separate Claude plan limits
author: Mark Kinkade

marketplace.tagline: Session status for any model, with Claude plan limits
marketplace.longDescription:
A chip strip in Nimbalyst's bottom panel describes the focused session across Claude Code, ChatGPT/Codex, Copilot, Cursor and custom providers. Model names use supplied catalog names or readable IDs, with exact requested and last-observed served identities in the tooltip. Claude reply versions are parsed without a version table; a disagreeing or stale identity says Last reply. Configured effort distinguishes session settings from applicable defaults. Unknown or unsupported readings explain what is missing.

Workspace policy keeps Ask, Allow all, Bypass and Agent-verified distinct from provider approval, sandbox, filesystem and network restrictions. Effective session restrictions remain explicitly unavailable on the current host. Directory, branch and uncommitted-file count work independently of model support. Current context uses reported occupancy and capacity, including a valid zero. Available input/output or total counters stay visible without a percentage; tooltips separate cumulative, cache and reasoning counts without turning absent values into zero.

The plan chips report Claude allowances only: 5-hour, 7-day and model-scoped caps such as 7d Fable. Beside another or unknown provider they relabel to Claude 5h / Claude 7d and render muted. These readings come from the Claude login/config source; association with the selected session's account is unverified. No other provider's quota is reported. Real fixtures cover Claude and Codex; Copilot/Cursor capabilities are source-verified, and custom/future cases have automated fallback coverage. The gear picks visible chips and their order, remembered across workspaces.
highlights: Requested and last-observed served model identity, with catalog names and readable future IDs
Configured effort with labeled defaults, and workspace policy separate from session restrictions
Reported current context, plus separate cumulative, cache and reasoning token counters
Directory, git branch and dirty-file count independent of provider support
Claude plan limits, relabelled and muted beside another provider
Gear chip for segment visibility/order, plus Ctrl+Shift+S access
marketplace.changelog:
0.1.7: The model chip names the version that actually answered. A session records only an alias -- `opus` means whichever Opus is current -- so the version used to come from a table in the panel, which fell behind the day a model shipped and showed `Opus 5` in a session Opus 5.5 was answering. The chip now reads the model off the session's latest reply and works the family and version out from its id, so new versions read correctly without a panel update. Before a session's first reply it names only the family rather than guessing at a version, and its tooltip shows both the alias and the model that served it.
0.1.6: The strip stays up when you change modes. Nimbalyst closes every bottom panel each time the window mode is set, and nothing puts them back, so switching to Files Mode or Settings and returning to Agent Mode left the panel gone until you pressed Ctrl+Shift+S. It now notices and reopens itself. Closing it yourself still closes it -- by the shortcut or by its button in the gutter -- and it keeps out of the way while the terminal or another bottom panel has the space.
0.1.5: The gear popover now names the version you are running, so what you have and whether anything newer exists are answerable in the same place. When a newer release is known it shows both, as `0.1.5 → 0.1.6 available`.
0.1.4: The panel now tells you when a newer release is out. Nimbalyst never updates a GitHub-installed extension on its own, so an Update chip appears at the end of the strip when this repo has published a newer version, offering to install it -- always behind a confirmation, never automatically, and with the manual paste-the-URL path beside it. It asks GitHub at most once every few hours, shows nothing at all when it cannot ask, and switches off entirely under Behavior in the gear popover. Also in this release: every segment with no data now says why instead of vanishing, a folder that is not a git repository says so rather than showing an empty branch chip, and both read legibly on the light theme.
0.1.3: Light and dark screenshots of the panel now ship in the README, in the extension listing and inside the package itself. No functional change. This is also the first published release to carry 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, which were only ever built locally.
0.1.2: Beside a session from another provider, the plan-limit chips now read `Claude 5h` in the muted accent instead of a full-saturation `5h`, with a tooltip naming that provider. The readings are unchanged — they were always about your Claude plan.
0.1.1: The published byline is now Mark Kinkade, matching the LICENSE; no functional change.
0.1.0: First release. Chip strip for the focused session with model, effort, permission mode, directory, branch, context usage and Claude plan limits, plus a configurable segment order. Claude Code sessions only.
